thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: KV cache surge detected for continuous-batching on prod cluster us-west-2. Error rate up and token latency spike > 3x. Please acknowledge.

alice (oncall): ack. I'm looking at dashboards now — token p95 jumped at 02:47 UTC, batch sizes spiked, and memory on a few inference pods climbed to 95%.
miguel: I'm seeing a correlation with speculative decoding traffic. There's a draft->target sync path that requests both draft and target KV prefixes. On heavy speculative flows that's duplicating prefix population and evicting older entries.
sasha: logs show a cascading cache re-populate loop: many small speculative requests generate new KV entries, which pushes out hot prefixes for longer-running requests. Continuous batching then aggregates more small requests into bigger batches and thrashes memory.
ben: we've got customer-facing errors: 5 customers hit 429s and timeouts on embedding routes routed to this cluster. CS is being triaged.
lisa (prod-eng): quick mitigation plan draft: 1) temporarily disable speculative decoding for the draft-only path (feature flag). 2) throttle continuous batching max_batch_size and max_window_ms for the affected pool. 3) trigger a targeted KV cache eviction for prefixes created in last 2m. 4) route traffic to fallback model variants in eu-west-1 if capacity allows.
alice (oncall): doing 1) and 2) now. Applying feature flag: `curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane/api/ff -d '{"spec_decoding_draft_only":false}'` (will revert later).
opsbot: flag update accepted. spec_decoding_draft_only=false on pool prod-usw2-batches.
miguel: running kv eviction job to scrub prefixes with tag speculative:true and age < 3m. Command: ```redwoodctl kv evict --pool prod-usw2-batches --selector "speculative:true" --max-age 180```
opsbot: eviction job queued (job id 6c3f).
sasha: lowering batching window: patch config `continuous_batching.max_batch_size=64 -> 32` and `continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=50 -> 25` for the pool to reduce aggregation of speculative fragments. Applying now via rollout: `curl -XPATCH https://controlplane/api/pools/prod-usw2-batches -d '{"continuous_batching": {"max_batch_size": 32, "max_wait_ms": 25}}'`
opsbot: pool config patch accepted; canary rolling to 10% nodes. Monitor for error rate regression.
ben: CS updated customers with temporary mitigation and ETA. They reported latency back to normal for 3 of 5 customers so far.
alice (oncall): observing memory and latency dropping on canary nodes. Error rates falling. Continuing roll to 100% over 10m.
miguel: note — root cause summary: speculative decoding created mirrored KV writes for draft and target contexts. Combined with continuous batching coalescing many small speculative requests into large batches, this produced rapid KV population which caused eviction pressure and cold misses for heavy tails. When hot prefixes were evicted, latency spiked and batches grew as requests retried.
lisa (prod-eng): follow-ups: - add counters to track speculative write ratio (spec_writes / total_kv_writes) - add a soft quota for speculative prefixes per tenant - update rollout safety to detect rapid kv_population rate and auto-throttle speculative feature flag.
sasha: also propose tuning the speculative path to write only if target differs from draft OR under a sampling window. That reduces duplicate prefix churn.
ben: customer impact note for incident report: 5 customers impacted, 2 with transient errors >1m, 3 with latency degradation up to 4x for short windows. No data leakage, KV entries are tenant-scoped.
alice (oncall): handoff to next oncall (miguel) at 03:47 UTC — I'll stay reachable for 15m for questions. Next steps: monitor for recurrence for 1h, validate evicted prefixes don't lead to long cold starts, and confirm rollback plan is ready.
miguel: taking handoff. I'll keep the feature flag off and apply throttles if I see any renewed kv_population spikes.
opsbot: incident status -> mitigated (partial). Postmortem required.
lisa (prod-eng): assigning postmortem owners: miguel (lead), sasha (runtime analysis), ben (customer impact), alice (oncall timeline). Draft due EOD tomorrow.
ben: adding playbook notes for future — small speculative writes should be de-duplicated on client side and server-side should avoid double-writes within 1s window per prefix.
miguel: recorded commands and telemetry: `kubectl logs --selector app=inference -n prod | grep kvcache | grep speculative` and exported `kvcache.metrics.speculative_write_rate` for graphing.
alice (oncall): closing paging loop in 5m. react :thumbsup: if you want me to keep it open.
sasha: :thumbsup: marking follow-ups in triage board.
opsbot: Incident thread archived to incidents channel with tags: kvcache, speculative-decoding, continuous-batching, mitigated.
